title: Correlation and diagnostic significance of CD4 T cell subsets and NLRP3 inflammasome in ulcerative colitis: the role of the NLRP3/T-bet/GATA3 axis.
authors: Hu, Yingnan; Tang, Jingyi; Yu, Dian; Su, Shuo; Fang, Jintao; Xia, Linying; Xu, Wenjun; Zhu, Weihan; Song, Ninping; Wang, Fengyong; Diao, Dechang; Zhang, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究溃疡性结肠炎中CD4 T细胞亚群与NLRP3炎症小体的相关性及诊断价值，虽涉及T-bet/GATA3转录因子，但核心是免疫病理与临床诊断，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅用分子对接辅助验证，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is characterized by complex immunological interactions involving CD4 T cell subsets and the NLRP3 inflammasome, which influence inflammatory responses. This investigation focused on delineating the activation profiles of these components and their correlation with disease severity and activity, assessing their diagnostic implications in UC. METHODS: We conducted immunohistochemistry and ELISA assays to measure markers expression of CD4 T cell subsets and the NLRP3 inflammasome in UC patients versus controls. Findings were validated using correlation analysis, molecular docking and ROC curves. RESULTS: UC patients displayed increased Th1 (T-bet, TNF-alpha), Th2 (GATA3, IL-6), and Th17 (RORgammat, IL-17, IL-22, IL-23) markers versus controls. Additionally, Th1 and Th2 cytokines (IL-2 and IL-4) were significantly elevated in severe UC, while Treg markers (FOXP3, IL-10, TGF-beta1) were elevated only in mild-to-moderate UC. Enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, indicated by elevated NLRP3, Caspase-1, and IL-1beta levels. These molecular patterns, confirmed through correlation analysis and molecular docking, underscored strong correlations among NLRP3, T-bet, and GATA3, supporting the proposed NLRP3/T-bet/GATA3 axis. This axis, along with other biomarkers, showed strong associations with UC severity, Mayo score, UCEIS, demonstrated relatively high diagnostic value. CONCLUSION: The NLRP3/T-bet/GATA3 axis provides a referable strategy for multi-targeted combined treatment of UC and may serve as potential biomarkers for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and guiding therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）以涉及CD4 T细胞亚群和NLRP3炎症小体的复杂免疫相互作用为特征，这些相互作用影响炎症反应。本研究旨在描绘这些组分的激活谱及其与疾病严重程度和活动性的相关性，评估其在UC中的诊断意义。方法：我们采用免疫组织化学和ELISA法检测UC患者与对照组中CD4 T细胞亚群和NLRP3炎症小体标志物的表达。通过相关性分析、分子对接和ROC曲线验证研究结果。结果：与对照组相比，UC患者表现出Th1（T-bet、TNF-alpha）、Th2（GATA3、IL-6）和Th17（RORgammat、IL-17、IL-22、IL-23）标志物增加。此外，在重度UC中，Th1和Th2细胞因子（IL-2和IL-4）显著升高，而Treg标志物（FOXP3、IL-10、TGF-beta1）仅在轻至中度UC中升高。NLRP3炎症小体激活增强，表现为NLRP3、Caspase-1和IL-1beta水平升高。这些分子模式通过相关性分析和分子对接得到证实，强调了NLRP3、T-bet和GATA3之间的强相关性，支持所提出的NLRP3/T-bet/GATA3轴。该轴连同其他生物标志物，与UC严重程度、Mayo评分、UCEIS表现出强关联，并显示出相对较高的诊断价值。结论：NLRP3/T-bet/GATA3轴为UC的多靶点联合治疗提供了可参考的策略，并可能作为潜在生物标志物，用于提高诊断准确性和指导治疗。
